title: Build your own std::vector
tagline: Eight test-driven stages from an empty class to a vector with move semantics, the strong exception guarantee and insert/erase.
description: Implement my::vector<T> in a single header, one stage at a time, against a doctest suite that stops at the first failing stage. You manage raw storage and object lifetime by hand, grow geometrically, forward arguments into place, and make reallocation exception-safe. The same tests pass against std::vector, so they check only what the standard guarantees.

stages.title: Empty vector
stages.summary: Declare the class template and its size, capacity and empty observers so the toolchain loop works.

stages.title: push_back and storage
stages.summary: Manage raw storage, construct elements in place and destroy each exactly once.

stages.title: Reserve and geometric growth
stages.summary: Reallocate geometrically so push_back is amortized constant time, and add reserve.

stages.title: Copy and move
stages.summary: Implement the rule of five with a pointer-stealing noexcept move and a deep copy.

stages.title: emplace_back, pop_back, clear
stages.summary: Forward constructor arguments into uninitialized storage and remove elements.

stages.title: Strong exception safety
stages.summary: Make reallocation transactional and choose between copying and moving with move_if_noexcept.

stages.title: Iterators and member types
stages.summary: Expose contiguous iterators and the standard member typedefs so algorithms and ranges work.

stages.title: insert and erase
stages.summary: Shift elements in the middle of the buffer correctly, with aliasing and lifetime rules respected.
